core_obligations: Fix morphisms f : X -> Y and Y' -> Y of formal algebraic spaces and let f' : X' -> Y' be the base change of f (proof lines 6828-6829).
Identify the diagonal of f' with the base change of the diagonal of f along X' x_{Y'} X' -> X x_Y X (proof lines 6829-6831).
Check that every property of the diagonal occurring in the definition of the separation axioms is stable under base change (proof lines 6831-6833).
Conclude that each separation axiom holds for f' because it held for f (proof line 6833).
proof_roadmap: Set up the base change and its diagonal (proof lines 6828-6831).
Base-change stability of the diagonal properties used by the definition (proof lines 6831-6833).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that every separation axiom listed in the chapter's definition of a separated morphism of formal algebraic spaces is stable under base change (statement lines 6820-6824). The proof names the objects, observes that the diagonal of the base change is the base change of the diagonal along X' x_{Y'} X' -> X x_Y X, and records that each of the diagonal properties occurring in the definition is stable under base change, which proves the claim (proof lines 6827-6833). The level is H2 rather than H1: the argument is complete and displayed, but its real content is the identification of the diagonal of the base change, and the verification that each individual property on the list is base-change stable is delegated to the properties of morphisms it is read off from.
